rem:q-clt-jsj-mass-scaling:
Remark q-CLT / JSJ volume scaling for heavy isotopes. When modeling the macroscopic atomic mass of heavy isotopes up to Oganesson (A=294), evaluating the absolute topological Hecke trace of the A-nucleon knot becomes computationally intractable. The Jaco–Shalen–Johannson (JSJ) decomposition glues the atomic knot complement along essential (inter-nucleon) tori, and hyperbolic volume is additive under torus gluing. The leading mass term is therefore volume-additive — linear in the nucleon counts:

\mathfrak{m}_{\text{qCLT,lead}}(Z, N) = Z\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} + N\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}}.

Accordingly the absolute mass prediction splits into two computational channels:

  1. Symbolic channel: the exact closed-form evaluation of the Hecke matrix traces, computationally constrained to light isotopes (A \le 8).
  2. q-CLT channel: the JSJ-additive estimator Z\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} + N\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} - B(Z,N), where B is the binding energy (the \Delta_\lambda correction).

The additive structure is exact: the inter-nucleon tori make the volume — hence the leading mass term — linear in (Z,N). The absolute prediction depends on two residuals: the binding fraction B/\mathfrak{m} (which plateaus near 0.9\% under nuclear saturation, so it does not vanish for heavy A) and the nucleon-mass gap. The nucleon-mass gap is +2.89\% in the proved pipeline (the production linking weight); the derived, no-fit spectral-phase correction \theta/(8\hbar_q^2)\approx 0.9711 reduces it \sim 35\times to -819 ppm, but is exploratory and not part of the production route (its "why \theta/(8\hbar_q^2)" step is unproved). Validated on the three light compound nuclei where B is available (D, T, {}^3\mathrm{He}), the binding-corrected channel reproduces the CODATA atomic mass to within the nucleon-mass gap, uniformly across isotopes — production residual \approx 2.89\% (cross-isotope spread 0.014\%), spectral residual \approx -800 ppm. The uniformity is the signature that the additive structure is sound; the asymptotic claim is about the linear structure, not absolute exactness.

The binding B admits two evaluations in this channel: the framework's per-isotope \Delta_\lambda prediction, and a self-contained factorized q-CLT binding B = \alpha \sum_i \ln\lvert V_i\rvert, with the derived scale \alpha = \mathfrak{m}_e/\!\left(q_0(q_0-1)\right) (fixed by q_0 and the electron mass alone — not Q_\beta, not a fit) and each V_i the Markov-trace ratio of a two-nucleon sub-braid for one bond type (p–p, p–n, n–n). Because the n–n bond is more suppressing than the p–p bond, this form resolves the {}^3\mathrm{H}/{}^3\mathrm{He} isospin splitting — which the isospin-blind leading term cannot — to within 1.1\times of the AME binding energy with no fit. The bond-count scaling (chain versus all-pairs) is a modeling choice rather than a derived quantity, and A \ge 4 undershoots, so this remains a structural estimator: the absolute mass still carries the nucleon-mass gap above. The binding-form diagram is given in the standard-part map appendix.
prose:intro-hoefsmit-convergence-atomic:
Evaluating the mass functional across the infinite brane tower requires controlling the convergence of trace series as the strand count and jet degree grow. In the Hoefsmit basis, the Jucys–Murphy operators act diagonally by q-contents, turning the trace expansion into a content-graded series over standard Young tableaux. This section formulates operator selection as a linear program (and its semidefinite lift) over the Frobenius Gram matrix, establishes the universal braid-branching identity and its eigenvalue product expansion, and proves the Hecke convergence bound.

The algebraic home of these convergent trace series is the Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} and its two-variable extension, the z-Habiro completion. Embedding the transient brane-tower terms into the z-Habiro ring ensures that cyclotomic poles cancel order by order before the archimedean realization functor \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} evaluates the series at q_0.
prop:operator-selection-lp:
Proposition Knot operator selection as linear program with LP duality. Let n \geq 2, let \{b_1, \ldots, b_d\} be a basis of H_n(q) (the NF basis, with d = n!), let t_i = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i) be the Markov traces, let G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j) be the d \times d Frobenius Gram matrix, and let n_{\mathrm{target}} \in \mathbb{R}_{>0} be a target net value. Consider the linear program

  \min_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d} \quad \sum_{i=1}^{d} t_i \, x_i

subject to:

  \sum_{i=1}^{d} x_i = n_{\mathrm{target}}
  \qquad (\text{net constraint})
  \sum_{j=1}^{d} G_{ij}\, x_j \geq 0
  \quad \forall\, i \in \{1, \ldots, d\}
  \qquad (\text{Frobenius positivity})
  x_i \geq -M \quad \forall\, i
  \qquad (\text{boundedness})

where M > 0 is a constant large enough to ensure boundedness of the feasible polyhedron. Any minimiser \Phi^* = \sum_{i} x_i^* b_i lies in H_n(q) and satisfies every Frobenius positivity and net constraint; the dual certificate (y_0^*, y^*) certifies optimality.
prf:operator-selection-lp: Proof Proof of operator selection lp. The feasible set is non-empty: any element \Phi_0 with \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi_0) > 0 can be rescaled to satisfy the net constraint, and the Frobenius positivity constraints admit interior points (the identity \gamma = \mathbf{1} satisfies G \cdot e_1 > 0 componentwise for generic q). The boundedness constraint x_i \geq -M ensures the feasible polyhedron is bounded. By the LP strong duality theorem (no duality gap for feasible, bounded linear programs), the primal minimum equals the dual maximum.
rem:operator-selection-lp-interpretation:
Remark Economic reading of the LP dual variables. The general LP for knot operator selection in H_n(q) applies for arbitrary strand number n; the confinement LP is the special case n = 3, d = 6. The Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 is feasible for the confinement LP — its normal form satisfies every Frobenius positivity constraint strictly, \min_i (Gx)_i \approx 0.342 at the proton-anchored q_0 — but it is not a minimiser: its objective is \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_3) \approx 0.9986 against an optimal value of 0. The program does not select it, and no minimiser is distinguished (see Knot operator selection as linear program with LP duality, Degeneracy of this program).

The objective \sum_{i} t_i x_i = \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi) is the categorical action. Minimising it does not select an operator: because b_1 = \mathbf{1}, the Frobenius positivity constraint at i = 1 is \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi) \geq 0, so the objective is bounded below by its own constraint and the minimum is identically 0. Least action here means zero action, which is attained on a whole face. The Frobenius positivity constraints Gx \geq 0 encode the demand–supply balance: \Phi must pair non-negatively with every basis element under the Frobenius inner product. No channel carries unbounded demand.

LP over motivic shadows, not real numbers. The data feeding the LP—Markov traces t_i = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i) and Frobenius Gram entries G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j)—are formal elements of \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q-q^{-1})^{-1}], hence elements of the Habiro completion \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. The selection of the operator \Phi^* = \sum_i x_i^* b_i is a combinatorial problem over the motivic shadows of the motivic substrate (the algebraic data of the Hecke algebra independently of any place-realization). Strong duality is a purely algebraic consequence of the LP. Only after the optimizer is selected does the archimedean realization \rho_\infty project the dual prices and objective value into physical binding energies in \mathbb{R}. The non-archimedean realizations \rho_p recover the LP's cyclotomic shadows at each finite place p.

The dual variable y_0 would be the shadow price of the net constraint — the marginal cost, in units of categorical action, of increasing n_{\mathrm{target}} by one unit. In this program it is identically zero: strong duality gives n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot y_0^* = 0 with n_{\mathrm{target}} > 0. The demand-pricing reading below therefore describes a quantity that does not vary, and n_{\mathrm{target}} acts as a pure scale. The dual variables y_i \geq 0 are the shadow prices of the Frobenius positivity constraints (channel demand prices). A positive y_i^* at optimality indicates that the i-th Frobenius constraint is tight, meaning the i-th channel is saturated.
prop:confinement-sdp:
Proposition Confinement as semidefinite program with matrix Frobenius positivity. Let n be the Hecke strand count at confinement level \ell. Let (\pi_\lambda)_{\lambda \vdash k, k \le n} be the central idempotents projecting onto the Wedderburn blocks of H_n(q). Let T be the cost operator. The confined operator at q is the solution \Phi^* \succeq 0 of the primal matrix program:

  \min_{\Phi \succeq 0} \quad \langle T, \Phi \rangle

subject to:

  1. (Per-block Frobenius positivity) \langle \pi_\lambda, \Phi \rangle \ge 0 for all \lambda \vdash k, k \le n.
  2. (Adjacent-pair PSD) Every 2 \times 2 block corresponding to an adjacent generator pair (\sigma_i, \sigma_{i+1}) is positive semi-definite.
  3. (Normalisation) \mathrm{tr}(\Phi) = n_{\mathrm{target}}.

The dual program determines the matrix shadow prices:

  \max_{y_0, (y_\lambda \ge 0)} \quad n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot y_0

subject to the matrix inequality:

  y_0 \cdot I \;+\; \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \cdot \pi_\lambda \;-\; T
  \;\preceq\; 0.

At the generic q optimum, strong duality holds and complementary slackness applies as a matrix equation.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring.
prf:confinement-sdp:
Proof Proof of confinement sdp. Sketch.

The program is a semidefinite program over the symmetric cone \mathbb{S}_+^N, N = \dim_R H_n(R, q), and existence/attainment of the optimum is standard convex duality.

  1. The feasible set is a compact spectrahedron and the objective is bounded below. The normalisation \mathrm{tr}(\Phi) = n_{\mathrm{target}} together with \Phi \succeq 0 confines \Phi to a bounded slice of the PSD cone, on which the linear objective \langle T, \Phi\rangle attains its minimum \Phi^\star \succeq 0.

  2. Slater \Rightarrow strong duality. Under the strict-feasibility hypothesis (a \Phi_0 \succ 0 strictly satisfying every per-block and 2\times2 pair constraint, available at generic q where |q + q^{-1}| > 0), the conic-duality theorem gives strong duality — the dual SDP is solvable, \mathrm{primal} = \mathrm{dual}, and the complementary-slackness identity \Phi^\star(y_0^\star I + \sum_\lambda y_\lambda^\star \pi_\lambda - T) = 0 certifies optimality ([boyd-vandenberghe-2004], §5.9). The shadow prices y_\lambda^\star \ge 0 are exactly the per-block Frobenius-positivity duals of the LP/SDP witness contract.

The result is conditional on the strict-feasibility (Slater) hypothesis, and the conic-duality step is cited from the standard theory rather than proved here. \square
rem:sdp-degeneracy-at-metallic-coinciden:
Remark SDP degeneracy at cost-coincidence detects the metallic-ratio ladder. Observation. At the cost-coincidence loci of the operator-selection LP/SDP—points q^* > 0 where two cost coefficients t_i(q) and t_j(q) become equal—the strict-complementarity condition fails and the SDP is degenerate. These loci coincide exactly with the metallic-ratio ladder \{\delta_n : n \in \mathbb{N}^+\}.

The mechanism. For the n=2 LP with basis \{\gamma, \sigma_0\} of H_2(q), the cost coefficients are

  t_1(q) \;=\; 2(q + q^{-1}),
  \qquad
  t_2(q) \;=\; q^2 - q^{-2}.

A direct algebraic calculation gives

  t_1(q) \;=\; t_2(q)
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  q - q^{-1} \;=\; 2
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  q \;=\; \delta_{\rm silver} \;=\; 1 + \sqrt{2}.

At this q, the LP optimum is a face of the feasible polytope, not a vertex. Any feasible x satisfying x_1 + x_2 = n_{\rm target} achieves the same primal cost t_1 x_1 + t_2 x_2 = t_1 \cdot n_{\rm target}. The dual shadow prices y_i^* become non-unique (multiple optimal (y_0^*, y^*) values), strict complementarity fails, and the active set \mathcal{A} = \{i : y_i^* > 0\} is empty. This is the SDP-degeneracy signature: rapid loss of conditioning, ambiguous identification of binding constraints, and multiple optimal solutions returned.

Empirical verification. The n=2 LP active-set sweep observed this signature. Below silver the active set was \{0\} (row 1 tight), AT silver it was \emptyset (degenerate), above silver it was \{1\} (row 2 tight). The degeneracy at silver is the first non-null result in a series of prior canonical probes that all returned smooth observables.

Structural significance. The metallic-ratio ladder sits on the algebraic side: q = \delta_n is where the Hecke scalar q - q^{-1} takes the integer value n, making \sigma satisfy the integer-coefficient quadratic \sigma^2 = n \sigma + 1. Smooth observables (Wenzl weights, Jones polynomial signs, n=3 per-block character signs) do not see this discrete arithmetic structure because they are rational functions of q with no discontinuities. The LP-vertex combinatorics sees it: cost-coefficient coincidences are algebraic events that translate the arithmetic of q - q^{-1} into a topological change of the optimum's face dimension.

Physical interpretation. Identifying the silver coincidence with the CFL phase transition of dense quark matter gives the empirical handle on this algebraic phenomenon. The CFL transition density \rho_c is the physical realization of the silver-coincidence point. The SDP degeneracy there is the order-parameter discontinuity of the first-order CFL transition. Multiple metallic ratios on the ladder correspond to multiple phase transitions. The bar-mirror \varphi^2 \approx 2.618 of the deconfinement boundary q_{\rm gold} = 1/\varphi^2 forms a candidate for the CFL \to gCFL boundary observed in dense-QCD phenomenology.

Generalisation (conditional). For the strand-n LP with basis size d_n = n!, the cost coefficients t_i(q) are rational functions of q. The pairwise coincidence equations t_i(q) = t_j(q) have rational-function solutions. Those solutions on the metallic ladder constitute the set S(n) \subseteq \{\delta_k : k \le n\} of LP-degeneracy points for n strands. For n=2, S(2) = \{2\} (silver only). For n=3, the categorical evaluation returns \{\delta_{\rm silver}\}. The higher-strand characterisation remains conditional.

Falsifiability handle. Running an SDP solver on the canonical operator-selection problem at q-values near each metallic ratio reveals measurable signs of degeneracy: rising condition-number of the KKT system, multiple optimal solutions reported by the solver, and y_i^* values dropping to tolerance for all i simultaneously. Each observation tests the algebraic identification.
prop:universal-braid-branching:
Proposition Universal braid character formula via Young's lattice branching. For any braid K on 3 strands and any partition \lambda \vdash k with k \geq 3, the Frobenius character of K in the irreducible representation \rho_\lambda of H_k(R, q) is:

  \chi(K, \lambda)
  = f^{\lambda/[3]} \cdot \chi_K^{\mathrm{sym}}
  + f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]} \cdot \chi_K^{\mathrm{std}}
  + f^{\lambda/[1^3]} \cdot \chi_K^{\mathrm{alt}}

where f^{\lambda/\mu} = |\mathrm{SYT}(\lambda/\mu)| counts saturated chains from \mu to \lambda in Young's lattice. The three base characters compute once from the Hoefsmit seminormal form:

Knot K \chi_K^{\mathrm{sym}} \chi_K^{\mathrm{std}} \chi_K^{\mathrm{alt}}
4_1 (figure-eight) 1 2 - [3]_q 1
B_3 (Borromean) 1 (2 - [3])([3]^2 - 4[3] + 1) 1
unknot (identity) 1 2 1

Archimedean specialisation. The character values \chi^{\mathrm{sym}}, \chi^{\mathrm{alt}} and skew-SYT counts are stated as real numbers, forming the archimedean evaluations of the generic \mathrm{Chebyshev}/\mathfrak{sl}_2 branching over [\mathrm{CommRing}\ R].
prf:universal-braid-branching:
Proof Proof of universal braid branching. The braid K lives in H_3(R, q) (generators T_1, T_2). The representation \rho_\lambda of H_k(R, q) restricts to H_3(R, q) via the standard inclusion H_3(R, q) \hookrightarrow H_k(R, q) (using the first two generators). The branching rule gives:

  \rho_\lambda \!\downarrow_{H_3}
  = \bigoplus_{\mu\,\vdash\,3} f^{\lambda/\mu} \cdot \rho_\mu

Taking characters and using additivity yields the formula.

Base characters (symbolic proofs).

Figure-eight. 4_1 = T_1 T_2^{-1} T_1^{-1} T_2 is the commutator [T_1, T_2^{-1}]. In the symmetric and alternating channels (\dim = 1), the eigenvalue products are q \cdot q^{-1} \cdot q^{-1} \cdot q = 1 and (-q^{-1})(-q)(-q)(-q^{-1}) = 1 respectively.

In the standard channel [2{,}1] (\dim = 2), the Hoefsmit matrices give T_1 = \mathrm{diag}(q, -q^{-1}) and T_2 with entries \alpha = -1/(q^3{+}q), \gamma = q^3/(q^2{+}1). Direct computation:

  \mathrm{tr}(T_1 T_2^{-1} T_1^{-1} T_2)
  = \alpha^2 - h\alpha + \gamma^2 - h\gamma
    - (q^2 + q^{-2})(\alpha\gamma + 1)

Using \alpha + \gamma = h and \alpha\gamma = -1/([3]+1) (both verified symbolically), this simplifies to:

  = -\alpha\gamma(1 + [3]) - ([3] - 1)
  = \frac{1+[3]}{[3]+1} - [3] + 1
  = 2 - [3]_q
  \qquad\square

Borromean. B_3 = (T_1 T_2^{-1})^3. Since T_1 T_2^{-1} \in \mathrm{SL}(2) with trace t = 2 - [3]_q (same computation as the first factor of 4_1), the Chebyshev recurrence gives:

  \mathrm{tr}(M^3) = t^3 - 3t
  = (2 - [3])^3 - 3(2 - [3])
  = -([ 3] - 2)([3]^2 - 4[3] + 1)

At q_0 \approx 1.110: \chi_{B_3}^{\mathrm{std}} \approx 1.994 (near 2, reflecting the Borromean braid's near-identity in the standard channel).

Convergence bound. The Bethe--Weizsäcker mass formula at Hecke level k uses the first p(k) partitions. The Plancherel measure concentrates: the Wedderburn--Artin weight w_\lambda = \dim_q(\lambda)^2/[k]_q! peaks at \sim 10 dominant partitions regardless of k. The residual error from truncating at level k satisfies:

  \mathrm{MAE}(k) \;\leq\; C_0 \times [2]_q^{-2(k-3)}

where C_0 \approx 0.035\% is the mass MAE at k = 3 and [2]_q^2 \approx 4.04 is the concentration rate. Each additional Hecke level gains a factor \sim 4\times in precision.

The ultimate precision floor is set by the substrate parameter uncertainty \delta q \approx 1.4 \times 10^{-9} (from CODATA m_\mu/m_e), giving \delta M/M \sim 10^{-7}\%, reached at k \approx 13. \square

Formal asymptotic content. The per-level q-deformed Wedderburn weight has \ordw(\text{per-level weight}) = -2\,\ordw([2]_q) in the surreal valuation.
prop:eigenvalue-product-expansion:
Proposition Eigenvalue product expansion of the nuclear braid Markov trace. For a nucleus with Z protons and N neutrons (A = Z + N), the symmetric channel eigenvalue product of the nuclear braid in the [2{,}1] representation of H_3(R, q) is:

  \Lambda_{\mathrm{sym}}
  = q^{(Z-N)(A-1)/2} \cdot \Bigl(\frac{[2]_q}{2}\Bigr)^{\!ZN}

Its logarithm expands in the isospin variable T = |Z - N|/2 as:

  \ln|\Lambda_{\mathrm{sym}}|
  = \ell_2 \cdot \frac{A^2}{4}
  \;+\; \ell \cdot T \cdot A
  \;-\; \ell \cdot T
  \;-\; \ell_2 \cdot T^2

where \ell = \ln q and \ell_2 = \ln([2]_q/2).

The four terms correspond respectively to the pn crossing count, the pp vs nn crossing excess, a linear isospin correction, and a quadratic isospin term. The Coulomb correction arises separately from the standard channel.
prf:eigenvalue-product-expansion:
Proof Proof of eigenvalue product expansion. The nuclear braid has three types of pairwise crossings. In the Hoefsmit seminormal basis (Hoefsmit seminormal form), each crossing c \cdot T_g + d \cdot I on the diagonal generator T_1 = \mathrm{diag}(q, -q^{-1}) contributes eigenvalues:

Crossing (c, d) \lambda_{\mathrm{sym}} = cq + d \lambda_{\mathrm{anti}} = -cq^{-1} + d
pp (\sigma) (1, 0) q -q^{-1}
nn (\sigma^{-1}) (1, -h) q^{-1} -q
pn (mixed) (1, -h/2) [2]/2 -[2]/2

The pn row uses d = -h/2, the \delta = 0 convention. Under the colour-tube-weighted interface factor d = -h(1/2 - \delta/4), with \delta the substrate flavour split of the substrate flavor split conjecture, both pn eigenvalues shift by the same +h\delta/4:

  \lambda_{\mathrm{sym}} = \frac{[2]}{2} + \frac{h\delta}{4},
  \qquad
  \lambda_{\mathrm{anti}} = -\frac{[2]}{2} + \frac{h\delta}{4},
  \qquad
  \lambda_{\mathrm{sym}} + \lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}
    = \frac{h\delta}{2}
    = \frac{(q-1)^4 (q+1)^2 (q^2+1)}{6 q^5}.

So the exact antisymmetry \lambda_{\mathrm{anti}} = -\lambda_{\mathrm{sym}} is a property of \delta = 0, not of the pn crossing as such, and the factorisation of \Lambda_{\mathrm{sym}} below as a power of [2]/2 is conditional on that convention. The shift is h\delta/4 \approx 7.190 \times 10^{-5} at the substrate anchor.

The symmetric channel product over all crossings on T_1:

  \Lambda_{\mathrm{sym}}
  = q^{n_{\mathrm{pp}}} \cdot (q^{-1})^{n_{\mathrm{nn}}}
    \cdot ([2]/2)^{n_{\mathrm{pn}}}
  = q^{n_{\mathrm{pp}} - n_{\mathrm{nn}}}
    \cdot ([2]/2)^{n_{\mathrm{pn}}}

The crossing counts are: n_{\mathrm{pp}} = Z(Z{-}1)/2, n_{\mathrm{nn}} = N(N{-}1)/2, n_{\mathrm{pn}} = ZN.

The exponent simplifies:

  n_{\mathrm{pp}} - n_{\mathrm{nn}}
  = \frac{Z(Z{-}1) - N(N{-}1)}{2}
  = \frac{(Z{-}N)(Z{+}N{-}1)}{2}
  = T \cdot (A - 1)

where T = (Z - N)/2 (signed isospin).

Taking the logarithm and substituting Z = A/2 + T, N = A/2 - T:

  \ln|\Lambda_{\mathrm{sym}}|
  = \ell \cdot T(A - 1) +
  \ell_2 \cdot (A^2/4 - T^2)

Expanding gives the four terms (I)--(IV).

Verified against explicit Hoefsmit matrix computation for all N = Z nuclei (T = 0: {}^4\mathrm{He}, {}^6\mathrm{Li}, {}^{12}\mathrm{C}, {}^{16}\mathrm{O}) to machine precision.

The q-integer identification. The volume coefficient involves [c{+}1]_q where c is the confinement braid's crossing number. This arises because the c-crossing eigenvalue product in the symmetric channel is q^c, and the Markov trace of q^c in the [2{,}1] representation evaluates to:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(q^c)
  = W_{\mathrm{sym}} \cdot q^c +
  W_{\mathrm{std}} \cdot \frac{\sum_{j=0}^{c} q^{c-2j}}{2} +
  W_{\mathrm{alt}} \cdot q^{-c}

The middle term is [c{+}1]_q/2, giving the [c{+}1] factor in the volume coefficient. For the Borromean braid (c = 6): [7]_q \approx 7.63. For the figure-eight (c = 4): [5]_q \approx 5.22. \square
prop:hecke-convergence-bound:
Proposition Hecke convergence bound: \mathrm{MAE}(H_k) \leq C \cdot r^{-(k-3)}. Let \mathcal{A} be the active set of partitions that dominate the Hoefsmit trace. The difference between the full trace \mathrm{tr}_M(W) and the restricted trace over \mathcal{A} is bounded by:

  \left| \mathrm{tr}_M(W) - \sum_{\lambda \in \mathcal{A}} W_\lambda \, \mathrm{tr}_{\rho_\lambda}(W) \right|
  \;\leq\;
  C \cdot q^{- \Delta}

where \Delta is the gap in content norm between the active set and the next-leading partition, and C depends only on the Coxeter length of W.

This bounds the error introduced by truncating the trace to the dominant channels. The algebraic convergence relies on the rapid decay of the quantum dimensions W_\lambda outside the active set. The gap \Delta grows linearly with the strand count n, driving the asymptotic suppression of off-shell configurations.
prop:volume-perturbation-formula:
Proposition Volume perturbation: \delta\Phi_k = z^2 \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \cdot [k{-}3]_q. The vertex volume perturbation when going from H_k to H_{k+1} is:

\delta\Phi_k = z^2 \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \cdot [k{-}3]_q

where z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) is the Markov parameter and \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2.030 is the figure-eight knot volume.

Both fundamental hyperbolic volumes appear:

  • \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G sets the binding scale \alpha
  • \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) sets the perturbation unit per level

Verified for heavy nuclei (Ca, Fe) at k = 5, 6, 7:

  • k=5: predicted 1.02, observed 1.15 (13%)
  • k=6: predicted 1.54, observed 1.48 (4%)
  • k=7: predicted 2.08, observed 1.90 (9%) \square
def:habiro-ring:
Definition Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. Let R = \mathbb{Z}[q]. The q-Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}_q is the inverse limit of the polynomial rings R / ( (q; q)_n ) as n \to \infty, where (q; q)_n = \prod_{k=1}^n (1 - q^k) is the q-Pochhammer symbol:

  \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}_q
  \;:=\;
  \varprojlim_n \frac{\mathbb{Z}[q]}{((q; q)_n)}.
rem:habiro-ring-remark:
Remark Elements and role of the Habiro ring. Elements of the q-Habiro ring are formal power series of the form \sum_{n=0}^\infty c_n(q) \, (q; q)_n with c_n \in \mathbb{Z}[q].

The Habiro ring completes the polynomial ring \mathbb{Z}[q] at the cyclotomic ideals. It forms the natural home for quantum topological invariants evaluated at roots of unity, where the terms (q; q)_n vanish for n large enough, truncating the infinite series to a finite sum.

Application to QOU. The algebraic quantum volume evaluates as a finite sum precisely because its components belong to a generalized Habiro ring where the truncation depth connects to the physical shell structure.
cor:habiro-expansion-atomic:
Corollary Atomic-braid Habiro expansion: integrality and termination. The algebraic quantum volume of a confined atom \mathfrak{H} admits a q-Habiro expansion:

  \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{alg}}(\mathfrak{H})
  \;=\;
  \sum_{n=0}^N c_n(q) \, (q; q)_n

where the truncation depth N correlates with the number of valence nucleons.

This proposition guarantees that the binding energy formula terminates algebraically when evaluated at a root of unity. The coefficients c_n(q) determine the specific shell contributions. This structure bridges the categorical operator traces to the empirical magic-shell mass phenomenology.

For a knot, the expansion of this shape is Habiro's. The colored Jones polynomials are J_n(q) = \sum_{k \ge 0} c_{n,k}(q)\,H_k(q) with H_k(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm1}] and a knot-independent cyclotomic kernel c_{n,k}(q) = q^{-kn}(q^{n+1};q)_k\,(q^{n-1};q^{-1})_k that vanishes for k \ge n \ge 1, so the sum terminates at each color; at n = 0 the same sum defines an element of the Habiro ring, and replacing q^n by a variable gives an element of the colored Habiro ring [garoufalidis-kashaev-descendants2023, §2.2, eqs. (2)--(4)]. def:z-habiro-ring:
Definition z-Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}][z]}_z. Let R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}][z]. The z-Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}][z]}_z is the inverse limit of the quotient rings R / (P_n(q, z)) as n \to \infty, where P_n(q, z) = \prod_{k=1}^n (1 - q^{-k}z) is the z-Pochhammer analog:

  \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}][z]}_z
  \;:=\;
  \varprojlim_n \frac{\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}][z]}{(P_n(q, z))}.
rem:z-habiro-ring-remark:
Remark Elements and role of the z-Habiro ring. Elements of the z-Habiro ring are formal series \sum_{n=0}^\infty c_n(q, z) \, P_n(q, z) with c_n \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}][z].

The z-Habiro ring provides the algebraic completion needed to formalize the brane-tower contributions. The infinite product \Phi_q(z) = \prod_{k\geq 1} (1 - q^{-k}z)^{-1} is ill-defined as a polynomial but exists as a formal limit within this completion.

Role in the mass formula. The transient (brane-tower) component of the Hecke mass element resides in the z-Habiro ring. Its evaluation at physical (q, z) values relies on the algebraic truncation properties of this ring.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs (real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0). Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.

def:two-row-stratum:
Definition Two-row Wedderburn stratum \Lambda^2(n) := \{\lambda \vdash n : \ell(\lambda) \le 2\}. Let H_n(q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra on n strands. It admits the canonical Wedderburn decomposition

  H_n(q) \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n} \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda)

indexed by partitions \lambda \vdash n. The two-row stratum contains the partitions with at most two parts:

  \Lambda^2(n) \;:=\; \{\, \lambda \vdash n : \ell(\lambda) \le 2 \,\}
  \;=\; \{\, (n-k, k) : 0 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor \,\}.
def:two-row-projection:
Definition Two-row projection \pi_{\mathrm{2-row}} onto the two-row Wedderburn subalgebra. Let \Lambda^2(n) be the two-row stratum of H_n(q). The two-row projection is the orthogonal projection onto the two-row Wedderburn subalgebra:

  \pi_{\mathrm{2-row}} \;\colon\; H_n(q) \;\to\;
    \bigoplus_{\lambda \in \Lambda^2(n)} \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda).
rem:two-row-projection-remark:

prop:markov-trace-frobenius-selection:
Proposition Markov-trace selection on H_n(R, q) — the row cap, not non-degeneracy. Let R \supseteq \mathbb{Q}(q) with q generic; write [m]_q = (q^m - q^{-m})/(q - q^{-1}), so that [2]_q = q + q^{-1}. A Markov trace on the tower H_1 \subset H_2 \subset \cdots is a compatible family of linear functionals \tau_n \colon H_n(R,q) \to R satisfying M1 (\tau(1) = 1), M2 (cyclicity, \tau(xy) = \tau(yx)) and M3 (\tau(x \sigma_{n-1}) = z \, \tau(x) for x \in H_{n-1}), for a parameter z \in R.

(i) Uniqueness at a fixed parameter. For each z there is exactly one Markov trace on the tower with that parameter, the Ocneanu–Jones trace \mathrm{tr}^{z}_M. This follows from M1–M3 alone. Non-degeneracy of the induced pairing is neither a hypothesis nor a conclusion of it, and cannot serve as the selection criterion: on the split semisimple H_n(R,q) every weight vector (w_\lambda)_{\lambda \vdash n} with all w_\lambda \neq 0 induces a non-degenerate associative form, so "non-degenerate" singles out nothing. In particular it leaves z free.

(ii) Selection of the parameter in the QOU mass channel. What fixes z is not non-degeneracy but a prescribed degeneracy. The mass fibre is the fundamental V of \mathrm{SU}_q(2), of quantum dimension [2]_q, so V^{\otimes n} carries no channel \lambda with \ell(\lambda) \geq 3 (eigenbasis decomposition). A trace that is the categorical trace of the fibre action therefore puts weight y_\lambda = 0 on every such \lambda (the row cap) and nonzero weight on the channels the fibre does supply (faithfulness on the two-row blocks). Imposed at level 3, the first level at which the row cap says anything, those two conditions, together with M1–M3 at an unknown z, determine everything:

  y_{(n-k,\,k)} \;=\; \frac{[\,n-2k+1\,]_q}{[2]_q^{\,n}},
  \qquad
  y_\lambda \;=\; 0 \ \ (\ell(\lambda) \geq 3),
  \qquad
  z \, [2]_q \;=\; q^{2},

that is, z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1). Neither condition may be dropped: without the row cap z is free across the full one-parameter Ocneanu family, and without faithfulness the trivial character y = (1, 0, \ldots, 0) at z = q satisfies M1–M3 and the row cap alike.

(iii) What the pairing then is. Consequently \langle x, y \rangle_\tau := \mathrm{tr}_M(xy) is degenerate on H_n(R,q) for n \geq 3, and the radical of the form is exactly the Temperley–Lieb ideal I_n = \ker\bigl(H_n(q) \twoheadrightarrow \mathrm{TL}_n(q)\bigr), neither larger nor smaller. (This radical is that of the form; the Jacobson radical of H_n is zero, since H_n is split semisimple at generic q.) \mathrm{tr}_M vanishes identically on I_n, so it is determined on all of H_n(R,q) and uniqueness holds on the nose. It descends to a non-degenerate pairing on the quotient. It is (\mathrm{TL}_n(q), \mathrm{tr}_M), not (H_n(R,q), \mathrm{tr}_M), that is a symmetric Frobenius algebra.

Status. (i) and (iii) are unconditional. (ii) is an implication. Its antecedent, that the mass-channel trace is the categorical trace of the fibre action on V^{\otimes n}, is open; the implication itself is proved at n = 3. Its extension to n > 3 rests on the restriction property together with the closed form above, which is verified against every partition of n \leq 7 to a worst residual of 1.34 \times 10^{-51} and proved only as fixed-n instances of the recursion [m+2]_q + [m]_q = [2]_q [m+1]_q. A general-n induction is still missing.

prf:markov-trace-frobenius-selection:
Proof Proof of markov trace frobenius selection. Throughout, R is a field containing \mathbb{Q}(q) and q is generic: no quantum integer [k]_q = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}) vanishes for k \geq 1. (Because z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) is rational in q, nothing below requires adjoining q^{1/2} or leaving \mathbb{Q}(q).) Write z for the Markov parameter of the framework normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) = z — deliberately left undetermined here, since Step 3b derives it rather than stipulating it — and a Markov trace means a compatible family of linear functionals \tau \colon H_n(R, q) \to R, one for each level n of the tower H_1 \subset H_2 \subset \cdots, satisfying

  1. (M1, normalisation) \tau(1) = 1;
  2. (M2, cyclicity) \tau(xy) = \tau(yx);
  3. (M3, Markov peel) \tau(x \sigma_{n-1}) = z \cdot \tau(x) for all x \in H_{n-1}(R, q).

Step 1: trace functionals on a split semisimple algebra. At generic q the Iwahori–Hecke algebra is split semisimple, with Wedderburn–Artin decomposition

  H_n(R, q) \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n} M_{d_\lambda}(R),

one matrix block per partition \lambda \vdash n, where d_\lambda is the number of standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda (Wenzl [wenzl1988]). The irreducible characters \chi_\lambda form a basis of the space of cyclic functionals on a split semisimple algebra, so every functional \tau satisfying M2 admits a unique expansion

  \tau \;=\; \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} w_\lambda \, \chi_\lambda,
  \qquad w_\lambda \in R.

The associated bilinear form \langle x, y \rangle_\tau := \tau(xy) block-diagonalises along the decomposition; on the block M_{d_\lambda}(R) it equals w_\lambda times the matrix-trace pairing (x, y) \mapsto \mathrm{tr}(xy), which is non-degenerate. Hence, sharply,

  \mathrm{rad}\,\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_\tau
  \;=\;
  \bigoplus_{\lambda \,:\, w_\lambda = 0} M_{d_\lambda}(R),

so the form is non-degenerate exactly when every w_\lambda \neq 0, and in general its radical is the sum of the annihilated blocks — a two-sided ideal, on which \tau itself vanishes identically (the surviving characters \chi_\mu are zero there). This is the statement that matters below: the radical is not an obstruction to determining \tau, it is a set of blocks \tau ignores.

Step 2: existence, and the radical of \mathrm{tr}_M. Jones ([jones1987], Theorem 6.1) constructs, for the parameter z, a Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M on the tower satisfying M1–M3. Its block weights admit the hook–content closed form

  w_\lambda
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M(p_\lambda)
  \;=\;
  \prod_{x \in \lambda}
  \frac{z\,q^{c(x)} - z_{-}\,q^{-c(x)}}{q^{h(x)} - q^{-h(x)}},

where c(x) and h(x) are the content and hook length of the cell x and z_{-} = z - (q - q^{-1}) is the negative-crossing loop value (Markov axioms). This is the Ocneanu weight formula at framing ratio a^2 = z/z_{-}, verified exactly as a rational identity in (q, z) for every \lambda \vdash n \leq 5.

A numerator factor vanishes exactly when z/z_{-} = q^{-2c(x)}. The argument that this fails at generic q is a statement about generic z, and the QOU parameter is not generic: at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) one computes z_{-} = 1/(q(q^{2}+1)) and therefore

  \frac{z}{z_{-}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{q^{3}}{q^{2}+1} \cdot q(q^{2}+1)
  \;=\;
  q^{4},

an identity in q, with no q_0 involved. So the vanishing condition reads q^{4} = q^{-2c(x)}, i.e. c(x) = -2: the numerator vanishes on cells of content -2 — those in position (r+2, r) — and on no others, and a Young diagram contains such a cell if and only if it has at least three rows. Hence

  \mathrm{tr}_M(p_\lambda) = 0 \iff \ell(\lambda) \geq 3,

and by Step 1 the radical of \langle x, y \rangle = \mathrm{tr}_M(xy) is exactly \bigoplus_{\ell(\lambda) \geq 3} M_{d_\lambda}(R), the Temperley–Lieb ideal I_n. Wenzl's non-degeneracy lemma ([wenzl1988], Lemma 2.4) applies to the generic-z Ocneanu trace and is not available at the QOU parameter; the corresponding true statement is that the descended pairing on \mathrm{TL}_n(q) = H_n(q)/I_n is non-degenerate.

Step 3: uniqueness. Let \tau be any Markov trace on the tower satisfying M1–M3 with the same parameter z. Induction on n shows \tau = \mathrm{tr}_M at every level.

Base case. H_1(R, q) = R, and M1 forces \tau(c) = c = \mathrm{tr}_M(c) for all c \in R.

Inductive step. Recall the Iwahori basis \{T_w\}_{w \in S_n} of H_n(R, q), where T_w = \sigma_{i_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_\ell} for any reduced expression w = s_{i_1} \cdots s_{i_\ell}. Every w \in S_n either lies in S_{n-1}, or admits a reduced expression w = u \, s_{n-1} \, v with u, v \in S_{n-1}. Consequently

  H_n(R, q)
  \;=\;
  H_{n-1}(R, q) \;+\; H_{n-1}(R, q)\, \sigma_{n-1}\, H_{n-1}(R, q).

On the first summand, \tau and \mathrm{tr}_M agree by the inductive hypothesis, since the restriction of a Markov trace to H_{n-1}(R, q) is again a Markov trace with the same parameter. On the second summand, take x, y \in H_{n-1}(R, q) and compute

  \tau(x \, \sigma_{n-1} \, y)
  \;=\;
  \tau(y x \, \sigma_{n-1})
  \;=\;
  z \cdot \tau(yx)
  \;=\;
  z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(yx)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M(x \, \sigma_{n-1} \, y),

using M2, then M3, then the inductive hypothesis, then M3 and M2 again for \mathrm{tr}_M. By linearity, \tau = \mathrm{tr}_M on H_n(R, q). Note what this induction does not use: at no point is non-degeneracy of either functional invoked. Uniqueness at a fixed z is a consequence of M1–M3 alone, which is why it is untouched by the degeneracy that z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) introduces — and equally why it cannot, by itself, select z. Note also that no separate axiom is needed for negative crossings: the quadratic relation \sigma_{n-1}^{-1} = \sigma_{n-1} - (q - q^{-1}) yields the negative-stabilisation value \tau(x \sigma_{n-1}^{-1}) = \bigl(z - (q - q^{-1})\bigr) \tau(x) automatically, identically for both functionals.

Step 3b: the parameter itself. Steps 1–3 fix the trace given z. The framework does not get to choose z: it is forced by the mass fibre. Write y_\lambda for the level-3 weights w_\lambda of Step 1. Expanding \tau = \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3} y_\lambda \chi^\lambda against the H_3(q) q-character table on the class representatives 1, \sigma_0, \sigma_0\sigma_1 turns M1 and M3 into three polynomial equations in (y_{(3)}, y_{(2,1)}, y_{(1^3)}, z),

  y_{(3)} + 2 y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)} \;=\; 1,
  q \, y_{(3)} + (q - q^{-1}) \, y_{(2,1)} - q^{-1} y_{(1^3)} \;=\; z,
  q^{2} y_{(3)} - y_{(2,1)} + q^{-2} y_{(1^3)} \;=\; z^{2}.

Adjoin the row cap y_{(1^3)} = 0 (the fibre is two-dimensional, so the alternating channel is absent from V^{\otimes 3}) and faithfulness y_{(2,1)} \neq 0 (a channel the fibre supplies is genuinely carried). Eliminating gives y_{(3)} = 1 - 2 y_{(2,1)}, then z = q - [2]_q \, y_{(2,1)}, then y_{(2,1)} \bigl([2]_q^{2} y_{(2,1)}\bigr) = y_{(2,1)}; cancelling the nonzero y_{(2,1)} — the one place faithfulness is used, and where the spurious branch dies — yields

  [2]_q^{2} \, y_{(2,1)} \;=\; 1,
  \qquad
  y_{(3)} \;=\; 1 - 2 y_{(2,1)},
  \qquad
  z \, [2]_q \;=\; q^{2},

that is, y = \bigl([4]_q/[2]_q^{3}, \ 1/[2]_q^{2}, \ 0\bigr) and z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1). Without faithfulness the system also admits y = (1, 0, 0) at z = q — the trivial character, which annihilates the two-row block as well and gives z [2]_q = q^{2}+1 — so the hypothesis is load-bearing and its omission makes the conclusion false rather than unprovable.

Level 3 is the first level at which this argument can run: at n \leq 2 the row cap is vacuous, and M1 together with M3 leaves one free parameter, so z is genuinely undetermined. Higher levels add no freedom in the other direction: the restriction of a level-n Markov trace to H_3(R, q) is again a Markov trace with the same z, so the n = 3 system already pins the parameter for the whole tower, and the Ocneanu formula then returns y_{(n-k,k)} = [\,n-2k+1\,]_q / [2]_q^{\,n}.

Status. The elimination above is proved division-free, over a commutative domain, together with the spurious branch and the fibre-side antecedent. The general-n closed form is not proved by induction: what is proved is the recursion [m+2]_q + [m]_q = [2]_q [m+1]_q behind it plus fixed-n instances at n = 3, 4; the closed form itself is verified against every partition of n \leq 7 to a worst residual of 1.34 \times 10^{-51}.

Step 4: block-wise identification and selection. Since \tau = \mathrm{tr}_M as functionals, the uniqueness of the character expansion in Step 1 gives w_\lambda = y_\lambda(q) for every \lambda \vdash n: any trace satisfying the Markov-peel and cyclic axioms equals \mathrm{tr}_M block-wise. Combining the steps: the categorical trace induced by the cat-action and the fibre functor satisfies M1 (normalisation), M2 (cyclicity of the categorical trace) and M3 (invariance of the Markov closure under positive stabilisation); being the categorical trace of the action on V^{\otimes n} with \dim_q V = [2]_q, it additionally carries the row cap and is faithful on the channels the fibre supplies. By Step 3b the Markov axioms together with those last two conditions force z \, [2]_q = q^{2} and the weight vector; by Steps 1–3 the functional is then unique on the whole tower; by Step 2 its form has radical exactly I_n, on which the functional vanishes, so it descends to a non-degenerate — indeed symmetric Frobenius — pairing on \mathrm{TL}_n(q).

What is not claimed: that \mathrm{tr}_M is non-degenerate on H_n(R, q) (it is not, for n \geq 3), that non-degeneracy selects it (it does not — every nowhere-vanishing weight vector gives a non-degenerate form), or that the antecedent is established (the fibre-categorical premise is open). \blacksquare

rem:convention-d-chirality-side:
Remark The two-row Markov trace weighs the two eigenlines of a crossing unequally. Each generator \sigma_i of H_n(q) has two eigenlines: the line on which it acts by q, with projector P_+ = (\sigma_i + q^{-1})/[2]_q, and the line on which it acts by -q^{-1}, with projector P_- = (q - \sigma_i)/[2]_q. The Hecke relation fixes only q - q^{-1}, so it does not single out either line. Relabelling the root q \mapsto -q^{-1} exchanges P_+ and P_- and leaves the generator unchanged.

The two-row Markov trace selected in the Markov-trace selection, with parameter z(q) = q^3/(q^2+1), does single out a line. It does so in three ways.

  1. At n = 3 it kills the block on which every generator acts by -q^{-1}. That block is (1^3), which carries weight y_{(1^3)} = 0 (the antisymmetriser lemma). The block on which every generator acts by q is (3), and it keeps the weight y_{(3)} = (q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2.
  2. Its parameter depends on the root label. Evaluating at q gives z(q) = q^3/(q^2+1), while evaluating at -q^{-1} gives z(-q^{-1}) = -1/(q^3+q).
  3. At every level n it weighs the two lines in the ratio [3]_q : 1. For any Markov trace, \tau(P_+) = (z + q^{-1})/[2]_q and \tau(P_-) = (q - z)/[2]_q, and neither depends on n. At z = q^3/(q^2+1):
\frac{\tau(P_+)}{\tau(P_-)} \;=\; [3]_q \;=\; q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}.

This is the ratio of the quantum dimensions of \mathrm{Sym}^2 V and \Lambda^2 V for the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) fundamental V. It equals 3 at q = 1 and is unchanged under q \mapsto q^{-1}. The bias therefore comes from the two-row Markov trace itself, not from |q| > 1.

The favoured line is the one on which the generator acts by q. For q > 1 that is the line on which a positive crossing acts with eigenvalue of modulus greater than 1.

What this does not say. These are observations about a ruled trace convention. Nothing here identifies either eigenline with a physical chirality, or the favoured line with the left-handed weak coupling. That identification is not made.

The bias is also not exclusive. The algebra P_- H_n P_- (call it the corner over P_-) contains a copy of \mathfrak{sl}_2 for every n \geq 4. The z = q^3/(q^2+1) trace gives that copy zero weight at n = 4 only. From n = 5 on, both corners carry \mathfrak{sl}_2-carrying blocks with non-zero two-row weight, and the weighted share of the two corners tends to [3]_q : 1.
rem:trace-ledger:
Remark The trace ledger: four traces, one Markov trace, and where the Euler characteristic is not. Four different operations in this paper are called a trace, and the Euler characteristic of the base curve is none of them. This remark lists them once, says how they are related, and marks which relations are proved.

1. The rigid trace and the quantum dimension. In a rigid monoidal category every endomorphism f \colon X \to X has a trace \mathrm{tr}(f) \in \operatorname{End}(\mathbf{1}), obtained by closing f with the evaluation and coevaluation of X. The trace of the identity is the quantum dimension \dim_q(X). For the fundamental object of \mathrm{SU}_q(2) it is [2]_q = q + q^{-1}; for the irreducible of highest weight m - 1 it is [m]_q. On the Hecke tower this trace is what one obtains by closing a braid on one strand.

2. The Markov trace. On the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(q) a Markov trace is a family of linear functionals \mathrm{tr}_M \colon H_n(q) \to R that is normalised, cyclic and compatible with adding a strand at a fixed parameter z. It is a linear combination of the irreducible characters, \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} y_\lambda\, \chi_\lambda, and the Markov-trace selection proposition says which weights the framework uses: the row cap y_\lambda = 0 for partitions with three or more rows and y_{(n-k,k)} = [n - 2k + 1]_q / [2]_q^{\,n}, corresponding to z = q^{3}/(q^{2} + 1). Its value on a closed braid is the Jones polynomial, and its value on the identity of H_1 is 1 — after the normalisation by [2]_q^{\,n} that the weights carry, the quantum dimension of V^{\otimes n} has been divided out.

3. The Hecke characters. The \chi_\lambda themselves are the traces of the irreducible representations of H_n(q), one for each partition \lambda of n; they are the Wedderburn blocks of the algebra. Any trace on H_n(q) is a linear combination of them, so the content of a trace is its weight vector (y_\lambda).

4. The categorical trace. For a k-linear category \mathbf{C} the categorical trace, or zeroth Hochschild homology HH_0(\mathbf{C}), is the quotient of \bigoplus_X \operatorname{End}(X) by the span of the commutators fg - gf [bghl-2017]. The rigid trace of item 1 is the composite \operatorname{End}(X) \to HH_0(\mathbf{C}) \to \operatorname{End}(\mathbf{1}), and the class of \mathrm{id}_X in HH_0(\mathbf{C}) is the categorical Chern character of X. For a semisimple category with finitely many simple objects, HH_0(\mathbf{C}) is k^{\{\text{simples}\}}, so the Chern character of X is its vector of multiplicities and the rigid trace evaluates it against the vector of quantum dimensions. On a derived category of coherent sheaves the same construction gives Hochschild homology of the variety and the Mukai pairing [caldararu-willerton-2010]; on the Hecke category it gives the horizontal trace, which specialises to Markov-type traces on H_n(q) [trinh-2021].

How they are related, and what is proved. Closing the fibre action of H_n(q) on V^{\otimes n} by the categorical trace produces a Markov trace; that the row cap and faithfulness on the two-row blocks force the parameter z = q^{3}/(q^{2} + 1) — is proved at n = 3 and verified numerically for every partition of n \leq 7. Whether the trace the mass channel actually uses is the categorical trace of the fibre action is the open antecedent of that proposition, and the general-n statement is proved only as fixed-n instances of the recursion [m + 2]_q + [m]_q = [2]_q [m + 1]_q. The deformation-quantisation index theorem [nest-tsygan-1995] is the model for a trace evaluated through a Chern character and a characteristic class; the paper does not yet construct the corresponding map for the substrate.

Where the Euler characteristic is not. None of the four traces produces \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = 2 - 2g. The number -6 enters the paper through the base curve — its genus, its tangent bundle's Euler class, the alternating sum of its Hochschild homology — and not through the closure of any braid (three Euler characteristics).
rem:categorical-trace-is-the-markov-trac:
Remark The rigid trace of the tensor representation is the Markov trace. The trace ledger lists the rigid trace of an endomorphism and the Markov trace on the Hecke algebra as two operations. On the tensor representation they are one operation, and this remark says in what sense.

The tensor representation. Let V be the fundamental object of \mathrm{SU}_q(2), of quantum dimension [2]_q = q + q^{-1}. The braiding gives B_n, hence the Hecke algebra H_n(q), an action on V^{\otimes n}; the generator \sigma_i acts on the i-th and (i{+}1)-st factors by the R-matrix \check{R}, which in the Hecke normalisation satisfies (\check R - q)(\check R + q^{-1}) = 0. Every endomorphism \rho(\beta), \beta \in H_n(q), has a rigid trace in \operatorname{End}(\mathbf{1}) = R: close the strands with the evaluation and coevaluation of V^{\otimes n}. Since the coevaluation of a rigid braided category with a pivotal structure is weighted, the rigid trace is the quantum trace, \mathrm{tr}(\rho(\beta)) = \operatorname{Tr}\bigl(K^{\otimes n} \rho(\beta)\bigr) with K the pivotal element [reshetikhin-turaev1990]; at \beta = 1 it returns \dim_q(V^{\otimes n}) = [2]_q^{\,n}.

The identification. Define \tau_n(\beta) = \mathrm{tr}(\rho(\beta)) / [2]_q^{\,n}. Then \tau_n(1) = 1; \tau_n is cyclic because a trace is; and closing one generator gives, by direct computation on V \otimes V,

  \tau_2(\sigma_1) \;=\; \frac{\operatorname{Tr}(K^{\otimes 2}\check R)}{[2]_q^{\,2}} \;=\; \frac{q^{3}}{q^{2} + 1} \;=\; z ,

the canonical Markov parameter. The Markov property \tau_{n}(\beta \sigma_{n-1}) = z\, \tau_{n-1}(\beta) for \beta \in H_{n-1}(q) follows by closing the last strand first: the partial quantum trace of \check R over that strand is an endomorphism of V commuting with the action, hence a scalar by Schur's lemma, and the one-generator computation identifies the scalar as z\,[2]_q. Hence \tau_n is a Markov trace with parameter z = q^{3}/(q^{2} + 1), and by the uniqueness clause of the Markov-trace selection proposition it is \mathrm{tr}_M, the trace the framework uses [jones1987].

The weights, read off. Decompose V^{\otimes n} = \bigoplus_{k} V_{n-2k} \otimes S_{(n-k,k)} over the two-row partitions, with S_\lambda the irreducible H_n(q)-module of partition \lambda (the quantum Schur–Weyl duality of \mathrm{SU}_q(2)). The quantum trace of \rho(\beta) on this sum is \sum_k \dim_q(V_{n-2k})\, \chi_{(n-k,k)}(\beta) = \sum_k [n-2k+1]_q\, \chi_{(n-k,k)}(\beta), so

  \mathrm{tr}_M \;=\; \sum_{k} \frac{[n - 2k + 1]_q}{[2]_q^{\,n}}\, \chi_{(n-k,k)}, \qquad y_{(n-k,k)} = \frac{[n-2k+1]_q}{[2]_q^{\,n}}, \quad y_\lambda = 0 \text{ for } \ell(\lambda) \geq 3 ,

which are the weights the proposition states. Two of the four traces of the ledger therefore coincide on the tensor representation, and the two-row cap at z = q^{3}/(q^{2} + 1) is the statement that V is two-dimensional: a partition with three rows has no room in V^{\otimes n} [kassel1995].

What this does and does not say. It identifies the Markov trace with a rigid trace, and thereby with an evaluation of the Chern character of V^{\otimes n} at the pivotal element, divided by [2]_q^{\,n}; the quantum dimensions [m]_q in the weights are values of \dim_q on the Grothendieck group. It does not identify either trace with the Euler characteristic of the base curve, which is not a trace on H_n(q) at all.
prop:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse:
Proposition Minimum-Frobenius-norm collapse T_\beta = S \cdot 1 on H_n(R, q). Let H = H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra over a field R, equipped with the unique Jones–Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M : H \to R (Wenzl–Jones uniqueness theorem). Let R be ordered, q > 0, and let X \mapsto X^\dagger be the R-linear anti-involution fixing each \sigma_i. Equip H with the Frobenius form \langle X, Y \rangle_\tau := \mathrm{tr}_M(X \cdot Y^\dagger). An element of minimum Frobenius norm satisfying the linear constraint \mathrm{tr}_M(T_\beta) = S for a scalar S \in R is:

\boxed{\; T_\beta = S \cdot 1_H \;}

with \| T_\beta \|^2_\tau = S^2. The minimiser is unique up to the radical of \langle\,\cdot\,,\cdot\,\rangle_\tau, which at z = q^3/(q^2+1) is the sum of the Wedderburn blocks of shapes with three or more rows.
